issues.body: The module says "Forward secrecy is per-message via the ephemeral key." This is false for the implemented ephemeral-static X25519 sealed-box shape. A recorded WrappedSecret contains ephemeral_pub; if the recipient's long-term StaticSecret is later compromised, an attacker can run X25519(recipient_sk, ephemeral_pub), derive the same wrap key, and decrypt the historical ciphertext. This is an honesty-sensitive cryptographic overclaim in an externally unaudited surface.
issues.fix_hint: Remove the forward-secrecy claim and describe the actual property narrowly: a fresh ephemeral sender key and nonce are used per message, but compromise of the recipient private key compromises previously recorded wraps. Make the same correction in skills/e2ee-ng/SKILL.md, which repeats the claim.
issues.title: Ephemeral-static wrapping does not provide forward secrecy

verdict.summary: Round 7 regresses from round 6's clean review because the public wrapping documentation makes a false forward-secrecy claim. The construction is ephemeral-static X25519: each ciphertext carries the ephemeral public key, so later compromise of the recipient's long-term static secret allows recomputing every recorded ECDH shared secret and decrypting past wraps. Fresh sender ephemeral keys provide sender-side key independence, but not forward secrecy against recipient-key compromise. The implementation itself can remain, but the security claim must be corrected everywhere it appears.
